mainTopic: Learning Torah out loud and the humility that makes Torah last
overview: This amud praises learning Torah and explains what makes it last. It opens with ברוריה, who kicked a student for learning silently, and a ברייתא about a student of רבי אליעזר who whispered his learning and forgot it. שמואל tells רב יהודה to learn out loud, and also to enjoy this world's permitted pleasures while he can. רב gives similar advice to רב המנונא. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that Torah is a companion on the road and a cure for every part of the body. Several אמוראים then bring פסוקים showing that Torah must be on the lips, and רבא resolves a contradiction in one of those פסוקים. Next comes a series of teachings that link remembering Torah to humility, generosity and tireless review, with מדבר (the wilderness) as a key image. A story shows רבא humbly serving רב יוסף to make peace, and רבא then explains the journey from מדבר to הגיא as rising through humility and falling through pride. The amud ends by starting to compare Torah to a fig tree, a comparison that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ברוריה teaches that Torah must fill your whole body
steps.stepSummary: ברוריה kicks a student who was learning quietly. She explains from a פסוק that Torah is preserved only when it is 'arranged' in all 248 limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: She kicked him and said to him: Isn't it written, 'Arranged in everything and secure'? If the Torah is arranged in your 248 limbs, it is preserved. If not, it is not preserved.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a story that began on the previous amud. ברוריה rebukes a student who learned silently and uses a פסוק to show why that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She reads 'עֲרוּכָה בַכֹּל' as 'set up in ALL of you,' meaning every limb of your body. If you only learn in your head and your mouth is silent, the Torah is not 'arranged in everything,' so it will not be 'שְׁמוּרָה' (kept safe).

keyTerms.meaning: arranged in everything and secure (שמואל ב כג:ה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the practice of saying one's learning out loud rather than only reading with the eyes.

phrases.english: She kicked him,
phrases.notes: 'She' is ברוריה, from the story on the previous amud.

phrases.english: she said to him:
Is it not written like this:
"Arranged in everything and secure"?
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כג:ה

phrases.english: If it is arranged in your 248 limbs,
it is preserved,
and if not,
it is not preserved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the ברוריה story that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah stays with a person only when the whole body, including the mouth, takes part in learning.

steps.title: A student who whispered forgot his learning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a student of רבי אליעזר who learned in a whisper and forgot everything after three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר had a student who would learn in a whisper. After three years, he forgot his learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what ברוריה said. Here is a real case of quiet learning failing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברוריה gave the idea from a פסוק. This story shows the result in practice. Even a student of a great teacher like רבי אליעזר lost his learning because he did not say it aloud.
steps.whatToRemember: Quiet learning does not last. Learning out loud is what makes Torah stay with you.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer had one student
who would learn in a whisper.
After three years,
he forgot his learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ברוריה's teaching with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: ברוריה's claim that Torah not learned with the whole body is not preserved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a student of רבי אליעזר who learned in a whisper and forgot his learning.

steps.title: A sinful student spared because he served a great teacher
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא tells of a student of רבי אליעזר who was liable to burning before Heaven. The חכמים said to leave him because he had served a great person.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר had a student who became liable to burning before God. They said: Leave him alone. He served a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side story. The גמרא mentions it only because it is also about 'a student of רבי אליעזר,' just like the previous story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic here is not learning out loud. The link is simply the matching opening words. The lesson is that serving a great תלמיד חכם, called שימוש, carries great merit, enough to shield a person from a harsh punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: became liable to death by burning

steps.confusionAlert: This story is not part of the learning-out-loud discussion. It is placed here only because it also starts with 'a student of רבי אליעזר.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer had one student
who became liable to burning before God.
They said: Leave him alone,
he served a great person.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story linked to the previous step by the matching phrase 'a student of רבי אליעזר.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Serving a great תלמיד חכם brings merit that can protect a person from punishment.

steps.title: שמואל tells רב יהודה to learn out loud
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה to open his mouth when learning מקרא and משנה. He reads a פסוק as promising life to those who 'bring out' Torah with their mouths.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, open your mouth and read; open your mouth and learn. That way your learning will last in you and you will live long. As it says: 'For they are life to those who find them, and healing to all his flesh.' Do not read it as 'to those who find them,' but 'to those who bring them out with the mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main theme of learning out loud. It brings שמואל's advice, which matches what ברוריה taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל adds two promises: the learning will last, and the learner will live long. He uses an 'אל תקרי' reading, changing 'לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם' (those who find them) to 'לְמוֹצִיאֵיהֶם' (those who bring them out), meaning saying the words aloud.

keyTerms.meaning: sharp one (an affectionate nickname for a keen student)
do not read it as (a reading that changes the vowels)
to those who bring them out with the mouth

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברוריה and שמואל teach the same thing: say your learning out loud, and it will last and give you life.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the actual text of the פסוק. It adds an extra layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, open your mouth and read;
open your mouth and learn,
so that it will last in you
and you will live long,
as it says: "For they are life to those who find them
phrases.notes: משלי ד:כב

phrases.english: and healing to all his flesh."
Do not read "to those who find them"
but rather "to those who bring them out with the mouth."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to the theme of learning out loud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning out loud makes Torah last and brings long life.

steps.title: שמואל tells רב יהודה to enjoy this world while he can
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב יהודה to grab the chance to eat and drink. This world is like a wedding feast that soon ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: Sharp one, grab and eat, grab and drink. The world we are leaving is like a wedding feast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second piece of advice from שמואל to the same student. It comes in the same format, though on a different topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding feast is joyful but ends quickly. Whoever does not enjoy it while it lasts misses the chance. So שמואל says not to hold back from the permitted pleasures of this world, because life passes fast.
steps.whatToRemember: Life in this world is short, like a wedding feast. Use its permitted good things while you have them.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, grab and eat,
grab and drink,
for the world that we are leaving
is like a wedding feast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא, חֲטוֹף וֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second piece of advice from שמואל to רב יהודה, grouped with the first because of the same speaker and form.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoy this world's permitted pleasures, because life is short like a wedding feast.

steps.title: רב tells רב המנונא to use what he has now
steps.stepSummary: רב advises רב המנונא to spend his means on himself now. There is no pleasure after death, death does not wait, and no one knows whether he or his children will die first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רב המנונא: My son, if you have money, treat yourself well. There is no pleasure in the grave, and death does not delay. And if you say, 'I will save it for my children,' who can tell you the rule of the grave? People are like grasses of the field: some are blooming while others are wilting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching that matches שמואל's advice from the previous step. This time רב gives similar advice to his student רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב adds a point that שמואל did not make. He answers the excuse of saving everything for one's children. Nobody knows who will die first, since people are like grass, and some bloom while others wilt at the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: The grave, or the world of the dead
A fixed rule or decree, here meaning the order in which people die

steps.confusionAlert: This is not advice to waste money or to ignore one's children. It warns against denying yourself the basic good you can enjoy now, because of an uncertain future.

phrases.english: Rav said to Rav Hamnuna:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנִי אִם יֵשׁ לָךְ — הֵיטֵב לָךְ,
phrases.english: My son, if you have (means), do well for yourself,
phrases.notes: A paraphrase of בן סירא.

phrases.english: for there is no pleasure in the grave,
and death does not delay.
And if you say: I will leave it for my children —
who will tell you the rule of the grave (who dies first)?
People are like the grasses of the field:
these blossom and those wither.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to שמואל's advice to רב יהודה in step 5. It adds an answer to the 'save it for the children' excuse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoy your means now, because death is certain, its timing is unknown, and there is no pleasure after death.

steps.title: Torah as a companion for a lone traveler
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says that someone traveling without company should learn Torah. He reads 'לוית חן' as 'accompaniment'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Someone walking on the road with no companion should busy himself with Torah, as it says: 'For they are a graceful accompaniment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to praising Torah, continuing the theme of step 4 that Torah is 'life'. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that Torah can be a traveler's companion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'לוית חן' is a graceful wreath. רבי יהושע בן לוי hears in the word 'לוית' the word 'לויה', meaning escort or companion. So Torah escorts and protects a person who would otherwise travel alone and afraid.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is traveling on the road
Escort or companionship on a journey
Literally 'a graceful wreath'; here read as 'a graceful escort'
He should busy himself with Torah

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who walks on the road and has no companion with him —
should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'For they are a graceful accompaniment' (Mishlei 1:9).
phrases.notes: A play on words: לִוְיַת is read as לְוָיָה, an escort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the advice to enjoy life and returns to the praise of Torah from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lone traveler should learn Torah, because Torah acts as his escort.

steps.title: Torah as a cure for pain in every part of the body
steps.stepSummary: Continuing his teaching, רבי יהושע בן לוי lists pains in the head, throat, intestines, bones and whole body. For each one, the cure is Torah learning, and each is backed by a פסוק that mentions that body part.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his head hurts, he should learn Torah: 'a graceful wreath for your head.' If his throat hurts, he should learn Torah: 'and necklaces for your throat.' If his intestines hurt, he should learn Torah: 'it will be healing for your navel.' If his bones hurt, he should learn Torah: 'and marrow for your bones.' If his whole body hurts, he should learn Torah: 'and healing for all his flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי continues his list. He shows that Torah heals each part of the body, matching each body part to a פסוק that names it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same every time: find a פסוק about Torah that names a body part, and read it as healing that part. The list moves from specific parts (head, throat, stomach, bones) to the whole body. This sets up the next step, which builds on the final פסוק, 'ולכל בשרו מרפא'.

keyTerms.meaning: Navel; here standing for the inner organs
Moisture, or marrow, for the bones

phrases.english: If his head hurts, he should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'For they are a graceful wreath for your head.'
If his throat hurts, he should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'And necklaces for your throat.'
If his intestines hurt, he should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'It will be healing for your navel' (Mishlei 3:8).
If his bones hurt, he should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'And marrow for your bones.'
If his whole body hurts, he should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'And healing for all his flesh' (Mishlei 4:22).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching from protection on the road to healing every part of the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah learning brings healing to each part of the body and to the whole body.

steps.title: A human drug versus Torah, the drug of life
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריבי חייא contrasts human medicine, which helps one part of the body and harms another, with Torah, which heals the entire body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה son of רבי חייא said: Come and see that the way of people is not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He. With people, when a person gives his friend a medicine, it is good for this part and harmful for that part. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not like that. He gave the Torah to Israel, and it is a medicine of life for a person's whole body, as it says: 'And healing for all his flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב יהודה בריבי חייא, builds on the last פסוק of the previous step, 'ולכל בשרו מרפא'. He uses it to show how Torah is unlike any human remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea here is a contrast. Human medicine always has side effects: it heals one part of the body and hurts another. Torah has no side effects. It is a 'סם חיים' (drug of life) for the entire body at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see; introduces a striking observation
Flesh and blood, meaning human beings
A drug or medicine (it can also mean poison)

steps.whatToRemember: This whole section praises Torah as 'life'. It is a companion on the road, a cure for each part of the body, and, unlike human medicine, a drug of life for the entire body with no harmful side effects.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiya said:
Come and see,
that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:
a person gives a medicine to his friend —
it is good for this (part) and harmful for that (part).

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן:
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so:
He gave the Torah to Israel —
a medicine of life for one's entire body,
as it says: 'And healing for all his flesh.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בֹּא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the final פסוק of step 8 to draw a contrast between human medicine and Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike human medicine, which helps one part and harms another, Torah is a drug of life for the whole body.

steps.title: Torah is kept inside when it is spoken on the lips
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי explains a פסוק in משלי: Torah is pleasant when you keep it inside you, and you keep it inside you only when it is on your lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said: What does the פסוק mean, 'For it is pleasant if you keep them within you; let them be set together on your lips'? When are words of Torah pleasant? When you keep them inside you. And when do you keep them inside you? When they are set together on your lips.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אמי reads a פסוק as a chain: Torah is pleasant when you remember it, and you remember it only when you say it out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves: 'keep them within you' and 'on your lips'. רב אמי links them as cause and effect. Saying Torah aloud makes it stick in your memory, and Torah you remember is what feels sweet and pleasant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written: the standard opening for explaining a פסוק
You keep them in your belly, meaning you remember them deep inside you
They will be set firmly together

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings back the idea from ברוריה and שמואל that Torah has to be learned out loud, not just silently. The next three אמוראים (רבי זירא, רבי יצחק, רבא) each bring their own פסוק for this same point (steps 11–13).

phrases.english: Rav Ami said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"For it is pleasant if you keep them within you;
phrases.notes: משלי כב:יח

phrases.english: let them be firmly set together on your lips"
When are words of Torah pleasant?
When you keep them within you.
And when will you keep them within you?
When they are set together on your lips, meaning you say them aloud.
phrases.notes: The 'lips' = speaking the Torah out loud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of Torah learning from the earlier statements, now focusing on learning Torah out loud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is pleasant when it is remembered, and it is remembered only when it is spoken aloud.

steps.title: A second source: joy comes from the answer of one's mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a different פסוק for the same idea. A man has joy when he has an answer in his mouth. A second version says he has that joy when he knows the right word for the right time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We learn it from here: 'A man has joy in the answer of his mouth, and a word in its time, how good.' When does a man have joy? When an answer is in his mouth. Another version: When does a man have joy in the answer of his mouth? When 'a word in its time, how good' applies to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings his own פסוק to show the same idea as רב אמי: the reward of Torah is tied to having it in your mouth. The גמרא then gives two versions of how he read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the joy comes from simply having a Torah answer ready in your mouth, which happens when you learn out loud. In the second version, the joy of answering comes when you know how to give the right answer at the right moment. Both readings tie the reward to Torah that is spoken.

keyTerms.meaning: From here: introduces a different source for the same idea
A word in its proper time
Another version: a second way the teaching was reported

steps.confusionAlert: 'מֵהָכָא' does not mean רבי זירא disagrees with רב אמי about the idea. They agree on the lesson. He is only saying which פסוק he thinks teaches it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: It is learned from here:
"A man has joy in the answer of his mouth;
phrases.notes: משלי טו:כג

phrases.english: and a word in its proper time, how good it is"
When does a man have joy?
When there is an answer of Torah in his mouth.
Another version:
When does a man have joy in the answer of his mouth?
When 'a word in its proper time, how good it is' applies, meaning he knows the right answer for each moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same idea that רב אמי taught.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that the reward of Torah depends on having it in one's mouth

steps.title: A third source: Torah is close when it is in your mouth and heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings a פסוק from דברים: Torah is 'very close to you' when it is in your mouth and your heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: We learn it from here: 'For the matter is very close to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.' When is it close to you? When it is in your mouth and in your heart to do it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק brings a third פסוק for the same idea. Torah stays close to you when you say it with your mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says Torah is 'close' and also mentions 'your mouth'. רבי יצחק reads the mouth as the condition: Torah becomes truly close and part of you only when you speak it, and not only think it.

keyTerms.meaning: In your mouth and in your heart

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: It is learned from here:
"For the matter is very close to you,
phrases.notes: דברים ל:יד

phrases.english: in your mouth and in your heart, to do it"
When is it close to you?
When it is in your mouth and in your heart to do it, meaning you say your learning aloud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative פסוק for the same idea, after רבי זירא's.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that Torah stays with a person when it is spoken aloud
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים ל:יד, 'כי קרוב אליך הדבר מאד בפיך ובלבבך'

steps.title: A fourth source: the heart's desire is granted through the request of the lips
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a פסוק from תהלים‎: ה׳ gives a person his heart's desire when the words of his lips, meaning his spoken Torah, are not held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learn it from here: 'You gave him his heart's desire, and You did not hold back the request of his lips, סלה.' When did You give him his heart's desire? When You did not hold back the request of his lips, סלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a fourth and final פסוק for the same idea. A person gets his heart's desire, meaning success in Torah, when Torah is on his lips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the פסוק has a 'heart' half and a 'lips' half. רבא makes the lips the condition for the heart: when a person speaks words of Torah, he merits to have his inner desire for Torah fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: The request or speech of his lips
A word that closes a verse in תהלים, often understood as 'forever'

steps.whatToRemember: All four אמוראים (רב אמי, רבי זירא, רבי יצחק, רבא) teach one lesson with four different פסוקים: Torah must be said out loud. Speaking it makes it stick, brings joy, keeps it close, and earns the fulfillment of the heart's desire. Each one uses the same pattern: 'When does X happen? When Y (the mouth or lips) happens.'

phrases.english: Rava said: It is learned from here:
"You have given him his heart's desire,
phrases.notes: תהלים כא:ג

phrases.english: and the request of his lips You have not held back, Selah"
When have You given him his heart's desire?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֲרֶשֶׁת שְׂפָתָיו בַּל מָנַעְתָּ סֶּלָה.
phrases.english: When You have not held back the request of his lips, Selah, meaning when he speaks words of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the alternative פסוקים brought for the idea of speaking Torah aloud.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that speaking Torah aloud brings the reward of Torah
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים כא:ג, 'תאות לבו נתתה לו וארשת שפתיו בל מנעת סלה'

steps.title: רבא finds a contradiction inside one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the two halves of the same פסוק seem to clash. One half suggests a wish in the heart is enough. The other half suggests the request must be spoken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised a contradiction. It is written, 'You gave him his heart's desire.' And it is written, 'And You did not hold back the request of his lips, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the פסוק from step 13 and shows that its two halves seem to say different things. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half says God grants what is in a person's heart, even if he never says it. The second half stresses the request of his lips, which suggests that only spoken requests are answered. If the heart alone were enough, why mention the lips?

keyTerms.meaning: Raised a contradiction; set two sources against each other
The request of his lips; what he says out loud

steps.confusionAlert: In step 13 רבא used this same פסוק to teach about spoken Torah. Here he uses it for a new point. He is not repeating himself. He is now looking at a clash between the two halves of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rava raised a contradiction:
It is written: "His heart's desire You have given him."
phrases.notes: First half of the פסוק (תהלים כא:ג). The heart alone seems to be enough.

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the request of his lips
You have not withheld, Selah."
phrases.notes: Second half of the verse. This half stresses spoken words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the same פסוק from step 13 and finds a tension between its two halves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the פסוק in תהלים 21:3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a desire in the heart alone is granted, mentioning the request of the lips is unnecessary. If only spoken requests are granted, the first half seems wrong.

steps.title: Deserving people get their heart's wish, others get what they ask out loud
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction. Each half of the פסוק describes a different kind of person: one who is deserving and one who is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is deserving, 'You gave him his heart's desire.' If he is not deserving, at least 'You did not hold back the request of his lips, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. He explains that each half of the פסוק describes a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is זוכה, meaning deserving, does not even need to speak. God grants the wish of his heart. A person who is not deserving still has a way: when he asks out loud, his request is not refused. So the two halves do not clash. They describe two levels.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not deserving; he did not merit

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the פסוק are true. A deserving person gets even his unspoken wishes. A less deserving person gets what he asks for out loud.

phrases.english: If he is deserving: "His heart's desire You have given him."
If he is not deserving: "And the request of his lips
You have not withheld, Selah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two halves of the פסוק between two different kinds of people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the פסוק describe the same person and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first half describes a deserving person, whose heart's wish is granted. The second half describes a less deserving person, whose spoken request is granted.

steps.title: נצח, סלה and ועד mean forever
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב states a rule. Wherever the words נצח, סלה or ועד appear, they mean something that never stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: Every place where it says 'נצח', 'סלה' or 'ועד', it means there is never any stop to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק we just learned ends with the word סלה, so the גמרא brings a teaching about what that word means. It states the rule here, and the proofs come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching gives a fixed meaning to three Biblical words. Each one signals that something lasts forever without a break. Applied to our פסוק, God's answer to the request of the lips lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of; a ברייתא from that study hall
A word in תהלים that, by this teaching, means forever

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: A Sage of the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov taught:
Every place where it says
"Netzach," "Selah," or "Va'ed"
there is never any stop to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the word סלה at the end of the פסוק from step 15 and defines it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words נצח, סלה and ועד in the תנ״ך mean forever, without any break.

steps.title: Verses showing that each word means forever
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings one פסוק for each of the three words. In each פסוק the word stands next to 'לעולם' (forever), which shows that it has the same meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: נצח, as it is written: 'For I will not fight forever, and I will not be angry לנצח.' סלה, as it is written: 'As we heard, so we saw, in the city of ה׳ of Hosts, in the city of our God. God will establish it forever, סלה.' ועד, as it is written: 'ה׳ will reign forever ועד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its rule from step 16 by bringing a פסוק for each of the three words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיה, 'לנצח' is parallel to 'לעולם', so נצח means forever. In תהלים 48, 'סלה' comes right after 'עד עולם', so it continues the idea of forever. In שירת הים, 'ועד' is joined to 'לעולם', which shows it means eternity.

keyTerms.meaning: I will fight; I will argue
He will establish it; He will set it firmly
He will reign; He will be King

phrases.english: Netzach, as it is written:
"For I will not contend forever,
and I will not be angry eternally (lanetzach)."
phrases.notes: ישעיה נז:טז. לנצח is parallel to 'forever'.

phrases.english: Selah, as it is written:
"As we have heard, so have we seen
in the city of the Lord of Hosts, in the city of our God;
may God establish it forever, Selah."
phrases.notes: תהלים מח:ט. סלה continues the idea of 'forever'.

phrases.english: Va'ed, as it is written:
"The Lord shall reign forever and ever (va'ed)."
phrases.notes: שמות טו:יח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proofs for the rule stated in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that נצח, סלה and ועד mean never-ending
steps.whatToRemember: נצח, סלה and ועד all mean forever. Each one is proven by a פסוק where it appears alongside 'לעולם'.

steps.title: A humble scholar is like a loose necklace
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid listing the coming teachings, רבי אליעזר explains the פסוק 'וענקים לגרגרותיך'. A scholar who is easygoing and keeps a low profile, like a loose necklace that is barely seen, will keep his learning. If not, his learning will not last.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: necklaces, cheeks, tablets, engraved.) רבי אליעזר said: What does the פסוק 'And necklaces for your neck' mean? If a person makes himself like a necklace that hangs loosely on the neck, seen and yet not seen, his learning stays with him. If not, his learning does not stay with him.
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא gives a סימן, a memory aid that lists the next four teachings of רבי אליעזר. Then it brings the first one, about the necklace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loose necklace does not press on the neck, so a scholar should not press on others or be pushy. A necklace is partly covered by hair and clothes, so a scholar should not show himself off. This humility is the condition for keeping one's learning. Arrogance makes it slip away.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists coming teachings
A necklace; a chain worn on the neck
Seen and not seen; keeping a low profile
Stays with him; endures in his hand

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן is not part of רבי אליעזר's teaching. It is only a list of key words for the four teachings that come next, starting with this one, to help the learner remember their order.
steps.whyThisMatters: It opens a series of teachings by רבי אליעזר that link good character to remembering Torah. Humility is a condition for one's learning to last.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: Chains, cheeks, tablets, engraved.)
phrases.notes: A memory aid for the next four teachings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "And chains about your neck"?
phrases.notes: משלי א:ט

phrases.english: If a person makes himself
like this chain that hangs loosely on the neck,
phrases.notes: He is not pushy or a burden on others.

phrases.english: and is seen and not seen,
phrases.notes: He does not show himself off.

phrases.english: his learning endures with him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֵין תַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: And if not, his learning does not endure with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new series of teachings by רבי אליעזר about keeping one's Torah learning, continuing the daf's general theme of how Torah endures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar who is humble and not pushy, like a loose and partly hidden necklace, keeps his learning. An arrogant one does not.

steps.title: Humble like a garden bed, generous like perfume
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains the פסוק 'לחייו כערוגת הבושם'. Learning lasts for someone who lets everyone walk on him like a garden bed and who shares his learning with everyone the way perfume spreads its scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר said: What does the פסוק 'His cheeks are like a bed of spices' mean? If a person makes himself like a garden bed that everyone steps on, and like perfume that everyone enjoys, his learning will last. If not, his learning will not last.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives another teaching about what makes Torah learning last. He reads it from a פסוק in שיר השירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garden bed stands for humility: it does not object when people step on it. The perfume stands for generosity: its scent helps everyone nearby, not only the one wearing it. A scholar needs both traits for his learning to stay with him.

keyTerms.meaning: a garden bed, a planted strip of ground
his learning endures and stays with him

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "His cheeks are like a bed of spices"?
phrases.notes: שיר השירים ה:יג

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כַּעֲרוּגָה זוֹ
phrases.english: If a person makes himself like this garden bed
that everyone steps on,
phrases.notes: Humility: he lets others walk over him.

phrases.english: and like this perfume that everyone enjoys the scent of —
phrases.notes: Generosity: his learning benefits everyone.

phrases.english: his learning will last,
but if not, his learning will not last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next teaching in the same series by רבי אליעזר about how learning lasts. It follows 'וענקים לגרגרותיך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning lasts for a person who is humble like a trodden garden bed and generous like perfume that everyone enjoys.

steps.title: Cheeks like stone that never wears away
steps.stepSummary: Using a wordplay between לוחות (tablets) and לחיים (cheeks), רבי אליעזר teaches that learning lasts when a person keeps his cheeks working tirelessly, like stone that does not wear away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר said: What does 'tablets of stone' mean? If a person makes his cheeks like this stone that does not wear away, his learning will stay with him. If not, his learning will not stay with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a third teaching about lasting learning. He reads the word לוחות as if it hinted at לחיים, cheeks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stone does not wear down no matter how much it is used. In the same way, a learner must keep his mouth and cheeks busy reviewing, out loud and without growing tired. Steady, untiring effort is what makes the learning stick.

keyTerms.meaning: in his hand, in his possession

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer said:
phrases.notes: The parentheses mark a textual variant in the name.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of what is written: "Tablets of stone"?
phrases.notes: שמות לא:יח

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָדָם מֵשִׂים עַצְמוֹ אֶת לְחָיָיו
phrases.english: If a person makes his cheeks
phrases.notes: Wordplay: לוחות sounds like לחיים.

phrases.english: like this stone that does not wear away —
phrases.notes: He never tires of reviewing out loud.

phrases.english: his learning will stay with him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֵין תַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: but if not, his learning will not stay with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same series. The earlier steps were about character traits (humility, generosity), and this one is about tireless effort.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning lasts for one who keeps his cheeks working tirelessly at review, like stone that never wears away.

steps.title: If the first tablets had not been broken
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains 'חרות על הלוחות'. Had the first לוחות not been broken, the Torah would never have been forgotten from the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר said: What does 'engraved on the tablets' mean? If the first tablets had not been broken, the Torah would never have been forgotten from the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר moves from personal advice to a teaching about the whole nation. He explains what was lost when משה broke the first לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'חרות על הלוחות' describes the first לוחות, which were entirely the work of ה׳. Had they survived, the Torah would have stayed permanently 'engraved' in the people's hearts. Because they were broken, forgetting Torah became possible.

keyTerms.meaning: if only, had it been that
the first tablets (broken by משה after the golden calf)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "Engraved on the tablets"?
phrases.notes: שמות לב:טז, which is about the first tablets.

phrases.english: Had the first tablets not been broken —
the Torah would never have been forgotten from the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי (אֱלִיעֶזֶר): מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״חָרוּת עַל הַלּוּחוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Still on the theme of Torah lasting, and still about the לוחות. The focus shifts from the individual learner to the whole nation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Had the first לוחות remained whole, the Torah would never have been forgotten from Israel.

steps.title: Engraved means freedom from foreign rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב adds that had the first לוחות not been broken, no nation would ever have ruled over Israel. He reads חרות (engraved) as חירות (freedom).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: No nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says 'חרות'. Do not read it 'חרות' (engraved), but rather 'חירות' (freedom).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different lesson from the same word, 'חרות'. The unbroken לוחות would have brought freedom from foreign rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned that the Torah would not have been forgotten. רב אחא adds a political result: Israel would never have been ruled by any other nation. He gets this from re-reading the letters חרות with different vowels, as חירות.

keyTerms.meaning: nation and language, meaning any foreign people
do not read it as, a reading with different vowels

steps.confusionAlert: 'אַל תִּיקְרֵי' does not mean the written text of the פסוק is wrong or changed. It is a דרש technique that reads the same letters with different vowels to draw out an extra layer of meaning.
steps.whatToRemember: This series teaches what keeps Torah alive. On the personal level, it takes humility, generosity, and tireless review. On the national level, the broken first לוחות cost us both permanent memory of Torah and permanent freedom.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כׇּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן שׁוֹלֶטֶת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: no nation or tongue would have ruled over them,
phrases.notes: That is, had the first tablets not been broken.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Engraved" —
do not read it "engraved," but rather "freedom."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same word 'חרות' as step 21 to teach a further loss caused by the breaking of the first לוחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Had the first לוחות not been broken, no nation would have ruled over Israel. חרות should be read as חירות.

steps.title: Making yourself like a wilderness keeps your learning
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה explains 'וממדבר מתנה': whoever makes himself like a wilderness that everyone walks on keeps his learning. Whoever does not, loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: What does the פסוק 'And from the wilderness to מתנה' mean? If a person makes himself like this wilderness, which everyone walks on, his learning stays with him. If not, his learning does not stay with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching joins the list of 'what makes learning last.' רב מתנה reads a travel פסוק as a lesson about humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wilderness (מדבר) is open ground that anyone may walk over, and it never complains. The next word in the פסוק is מתנה, which means 'gift.' So a person who is that humble receives his learning as a gift that stays with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Wilderness, desert: open land everyone walks on
A place-name in the פסוק, read here as 'gift'
Trample on it, walk all over it
His learning stays with him and is not forgotten

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "And from the wilderness to Mattanah"?
phrases.notes: במדבר כא:יח. מתנה is a stop on the journey, but the word also means 'gift.'

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ כְּמִדְבָּר זֶה
phrases.english: If a person makes himself like this wilderness
which everyone treads upon,
his learning endures with him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֵין תַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: And if not, his learning does not endure with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching to the series on what makes Torah learning last. It parallels רבי אליעזר's 'garden bed that everyone walks on.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humility, meaning letting everyone 'walk on you' like a wilderness, makes Torah learning last.

steps.title: רבא humbly mixes רב יוסף's wine to make peace
steps.stepSummary: רבא had a falling-out with רב יוסף. On ערב יום כיפור he went to make peace, took the cup from the attendant, and mixed the wine himself. רב יוסף recognized his style and רבא said, 'It is I.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רב יוסף בר חמא had a falling-out with רב יוסף. When ערב יום כיפור came, he said: I will go and make peace with him. He went and found רב יוסף's attendant mixing him a cup of wine. He said: Give it to me and I will mix it. The attendant gave it to him, and he mixed it. When רב יוסף tasted it, he said: This mixing is like the mixing of רבא son of רב יוסף בר חמא. רבא said to him: It is I.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that acts out the humility it just taught. A great scholar takes the job of a servant to make peace with his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not wait for רב יוסף to come to him. He takes the lowly job of the attendant and serves his teacher, which is exactly 'making yourself like a wilderness.' רב יוסף was blind, so he recognized רבא only by his special way of mixing the wine with water. This story sets up the conversation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter; here, a grievance or falling-out
I will appease him, make peace with him
Mixing a cup (diluting wine with water)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two names here that look alike. רבא is the son of רב יוסף בר חמא, and רב יוסף (his teacher) is a different person. רבא's father is not the teacher he is appeasing.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Ḥama,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה לֵיהּ מִלְּתָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּהֲדֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef had a grievance with him.
When the eve of Yom Kippur arrived,
he said: I will go and appease him.
He went and found his attendant
mixing a cup of wine for him.
He said: Give it to me, and I will mix it.
He gave it to him, and he mixed it.
When Rav Yosef tasted it, he said:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף was blind, so he could not see who had mixed it.

phrases.english: This mixing is like the mixing

phrases.aramaic: דְּרָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא.
phrases.english: of Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Ḥama.
Rava said to him: It is I.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ מִלְּתָא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates רב מתנה's teaching about humility. It leads into a fuller reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story showing a great scholar humbling himself and serving his teacher in order to make peace.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks רבא to explain the chain of verses
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells רבא not to sit down until he explains the whole sequence: מדבר → מתנה → נחליאל → במות → הגיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Do not sit down until you explain these פסוקים to me. What is the meaning of what is written: 'And from the wilderness to מתנה, and from מתנה to נחליאל, and from נחליאל to במות, and from במות to the valley'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks רבא to explain a whole chain of place-names in the פסוק. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה explained only the first link, מדבר to מתנה. רב יוסף wants the meaning of the entire list of journey stops. The challenge to explain it on the spot also works as a welcome back into the teacher-student relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'don't sit on your legs'; don't sit down
A place-name in the פסוק, read as נחלו אל (God made it his inheritance)

phrases.english: He said to him: Do not sit down on your knees
until you explain these verses to me.
What is the meaning of what is written: "And from the wilderness to Mattanah,
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel,
and from Nahaliel to Bamoth, and from Bamoth to the valley"?
phrases.notes: במדבר כא:יט–כ.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּתֵּיב אַכַּרְעָיךָ עַד דִּמְפָרְשַׁתְּ לִי הָנֵי קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. Now that רבא has identified himself, רב יוסף asks him to interpret the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the full sequence of journey stops: מדבר, מתנה, נחליאל, במות, הגיא.

steps.title: רבא explains: humility, then gift, then inheritance, then greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains each stop as a stage. Humility like a wilderness brings Torah as a gift (מתנה). Then God makes it his inheritance (נחליאל). Then he rises to greatness (במות).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If a person makes himself like this wilderness, which everyone walks on, the Torah is given to him as a gift. Once it is given to him as a gift, God makes it his inheritance, as it says: 'And from מתנה to נחליאל.' Once God makes it his inheritance, he rises to greatness, as it says: 'And from נחליאל to במות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב יוסף by reading each place-name as a step up in spiritual growth. His answer continues next with the next stop, הגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא builds on רב מתנה's first link and turns the list of journey stops into a ladder. מתנה becomes 'gift,' נחליאל is read as נחלו אל ('God made it his inheritance'), and במות means 'heights,' meaning greatness. The whole climb begins with the humility of the wilderness, which is exactly what רבא himself just showed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is given to him as a gift
God made it his inheritance (wordplay on נחליאל)

steps.whyThisMatters: The story and the explanation fit together. רבא earns his teacher's welcome by acting like a 'wilderness,' and then he teaches that this very humility is the first step toward Torah and greatness.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם אָדָם מֵשִׂים עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: He said to him: If a person makes himself
like this wilderness, which everyone treads upon,
the Torah is given to him as a gift.
And once it is given to him as a gift,
God makes it his inheritance, as it is stated: "And from Mattanah to Nahaliel."
phrases.notes: נחליאל is split into נחלו + אל.

phrases.english: And once God has made it his inheritance, he rises to greatness,
as it is stated: "And from Nahaliel to Bamoth" (heights).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם אָדָם מֵשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּמִדְבָּר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question from the previous step. It extends רב מתנה's single link into a chain of stages.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each place-name is a stage. מדבר is humility, מתנה is Torah as a gift, נחליאל is God making it his inheritance, and במות is rising to greatness. The explanation of הגיא continues next.

steps.title: Pride brings him down; returning lifts him up
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his explanation. If the learner who has risen becomes proud, הקדוש ברוך הוא lowers him ('from במות to the valley'). If he does תשובה, הקדוש ברוך הוא raises him again ('every valley shall be lifted').
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he becomes proud, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings him down, as it says: 'And from Bamoth to the valley.' And if he takes it back, the Holy One, Blessed be He, lifts him up, as it says: 'Every valley shall be lifted up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer to רב יוסף by explaining the last stop on the list, הגיא (the valley).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the learner climbed all the way up to במות (the heights). Now רבא adds a warning: if those heights make him proud, he falls into the valley. A second פסוק from ישעיה promises that a valley can be raised, so even after a fall, תשובה brings him back up.

keyTerms.meaning: Valley (the last stop on the journey)

steps.whatToRemember: The full path is: humility (מדבר), then Torah as a gift (מתנה), then Torah as his inheritance (נחליאל), then greatness (במות). Pride brings him down to the valley (הגיא), and תשובה raises him again.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the whole מדבר-to-הגיא sequence that רב יוסף asked about in step 25. It ends on a hopeful note: a fall is not permanent.

phrases.english: And if he becomes proud,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, lowers him,
as it says: 'And from Bamoth to the valley.'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק from במדבר כא that the whole sequence comes from.

phrases.english: And if he takes it back (repents),
the Holy One, Blessed be He, lifts him up,
as it says: 'Every valley shall be lifted up.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה מ:ד

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מֵגֵיס לִבּוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁפִּילוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes רבא's answer from step 26 by explaining the final stop, הגיא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הגיא means that pride brings the great learner down. The added פסוק 'כל גיא ינשא' teaches that תשובה raises him again.

steps.title: Be like a wild animal that eats its catch right away
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads 'חיתך ישבו בה' as 'your animal'. A learner who acts like an animal that tramples its catch and eats it right away keeps his learning. Another version says: like an animal that dirties its food and eats it anyway. If he does this, הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself makes him a feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Your flock (חיה) dwelt in it; You prepare in Your goodness for the poor one, O God'? If a person makes himself like an animal that tramples and eats (and some say, that dirties its food and eats), his learning stays with him. If not, his learning does not stay with him. And if he does this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself makes him a feast, as it says: 'You prepare in Your goodness for the poor one, O God.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב הונא explains a פסוק in תהלים as a lesson about how to make your learning last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חַיָּתְךָ is read as חַיָּה, a wild animal. The first version says the animal eats its catch right away without waiting, so a learner should review what he heard immediately. The second version (מסרחת) says the animal is not fussy about dirtying its food, so a learner should not worry about his own honor while learning. The end of the פסוק ('for the poor one') is the reward: God prepares a feast for the one who makes himself humble like this.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the written verse mean?
Some say (another version of the teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: The animal comparison is not an insult. It praises a learner who is eager (reviews right away) or humble (does not care about his own honor). It fits the same humility theme as the מדבר teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: What is meant by what is written:
'Your flock (animal) dwelt in it;'
'You prepare in Your goodness for the poor one, O God'?
phrases.notes: תהלים סח:יא

phrases.english: If a person makes himself
like this animal that tramples and eats,
phrases.notes: It eats its catch right away, so a learner reviews immediately.

phrases.english: and some say,
(like an animal) that dirties its food and eats it,
phrases.notes: It is not fussy, so a learner does not worry about his own honor.

phrases.english: his learning stays with him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֵין תַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ.
phrases.english: And if not, his learning does not stay with him.
And if he does so,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ סְעוּדָה בְּעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, Himself makes him a feast,
as it says: 'You prepare in Your goodness for the poor one, O God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה on the same theme: what makes a person's Torah learning last.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A learner who reviews right away and is not fussy about his own honor keeps his learning, and God rewards him with a feast.

steps.title: Why Torah is compared to a fig tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, quotes 'He who guards the fig tree will eat its fruit' and asks why דברי תורה are compared to a fig tree. He begins the comparison: 'Just as this fig tree...'. The comparison continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק mean, 'He who guards the fig tree will eat its fruit'? Why were words of Torah compared to a fig tree? Just as this fig tree...
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The גמרא asks why Torah is compared to a fig tree and starts to answer, but the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי is read as being about Torah. The setup question (why a fig tree in particular?) means there must be something special about figs that teaches how to learn. The words 'מה תאנה זו' open the comparison, and its point comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: This step ends in the middle of a sentence. Do not look for the answer here. It continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is meant by what is written: 'He who guards the fig tree will eat its fruit'?
phrases.notes: משלי כז:יח

phrases.english: Why were words of Torah compared to a fig tree?
Just as this fig tree...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts another פסוק-based teaching about learning Torah, this time comparing Torah to a fig tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is compared to a fig tree. The reason begins with 'מה תאנה זו' and continues on the next amud.
